cultural_context.description: Kerala has a diverse cultural heritage expressed through classical and folk performing arts, ritual traditions, festivals, cuisine, literature, crafts, and community celebrations.
cultural_context.important_note: Cultural practices vary between regions, communities, religions, families, generations, and individual contexts. Information in this file should not be treated as universal to every person in Kerala.

source.title: Culture

communication_guidance: Use respectful communication when interacting with local people.
Do not assume that one communication style applies identically across Kerala's different communities and regions.
When participating in a cultural, religious, or ritual event, follow the guidance of local hosts, organizers, or the venue.

core_values.description: Government of Kerala material emphasizes responsible engagement with local artists, performers, craftspeople, and communities so that traditional art forms are respected and preserved.

festivals.name: Onam
festivals.period: Malayalam month of Chingam; dates vary by year
festivals.description: Onam is one of Kerala's most widely celebrated festivals. Kerala Tourism associates it with the homecoming of King Mahabali and documents traditions including pookalam flower arrangements, traditional performances, boat races, and sadya.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of Kerala
source.title: Kerala Cultural Festivals

festivals.name: Thrissur Pooram
festivals.description: Thrissur Pooram is a major festival of Thrissur. Kerala Tourism describes decorated elephants, rhythmic percussion performances called panchavadyam, and fireworks among its prominent features.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of Kerala
source.title: Kerala Cultural Festivals

festivals.name: Theyyam
festivals.period: Season varies by locality and temple tradition
festivals.description: Theyyam is a ritual art form particularly associated with northern Kerala. Kerala Tourism describes it as combining dance, mime and music and involving elaborate costumes and makeup.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of Kerala
source.title: Cultural Experience in Kerala

festivals.name: Aranmula Boat Race
festivals.period: Around the Onam season; date varies annually
festivals.description: The Aranmula Boat Race takes place on the Pamba River. Kerala Tourism describes it as a revered boat race associated with Aranmula and distinguishes its boats and rowing tradition from snake-boat races.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of Kerala
source.title: Kerala Cultural Festivals

festivals.name: Attukal Pongala
festivals.description: Attukal Pongala is an annual festival at Attukal Bhagavathy Temple in Thiruvananthapuram. Kerala Tourism describes it as an all-women observance involving preparation of a sweet porridge offering called pongala.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of Kerala
source.title: Kerala Cultural Festivals

traditional_dances.name: Kathakali
traditional_dances.description: Kathakali is a major Kerala performing art combining elements of dance, drama, music, elaborate makeup, and costume. Government of Kerala material identifies it as a prominent classical art form of the state.

source.organization: Government of Kerala
source.title: Economic Review 2020-21, Chapter 9: Art, Culture and Sports

traditional_dances.name: Mohiniyattam
traditional_dances.description: Mohiniyattam is a classical dance tradition associated with Kerala. Government of Kerala material identifies it among the state's established art forms.

source.organization: Government of Kerala
source.title: Economic Review 2020-21, Chapter 9: Art, Culture and Sports

traditional_dances.name: Theyyam
traditional_dances.description: Theyyam is a ritual performance tradition popular in northern Kerala, incorporating dance, mime, music, elaborate costumes, and makeup.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of Kerala
source.title: Cultural Experience in Kerala

traditional_dances.name: Thiruvathirakali
traditional_dances.description: Thiruvathirakali is documented among the folk arts of Kerala in Government of Kerala cultural material.

source.organization: Government of Kerala
source.title: Economic Review 2020-21, Chapter 9: Art, Culture and Sports

traditional_clothing.name: Traditional Kerala attire
traditional_clothing.description: Traditional attire is associated with Kerala's cultural and ceremonial life, but clothing practices vary by community, gender, region, occasion, and individual preference.

source.title: Kerala Cultural Festivals

traditional_arts.name: Kalamezhuthu
traditional_arts.description: Kalamezhuthu is a ritual art in which drawings are created on the floor using powder. Kerala Tourism describes it as associated with temples and ritual worship.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of Kerala
source.title: Cultural Experience in Kerala

traditional_arts.name: Padayani
traditional_arts.description: Padayani is a ritual art form celebrated mainly in central Kerala and is described by Kerala Tourism as being inspired by mythological dances.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of Kerala
source.title: Festivals

traditional_arts.name: Kalaripayattu
traditional_arts.description: Kalaripayattu is a traditional martial art associated with Kerala and is included by Government of Kerala material among the state's notable folk and cultural traditions.

spiritual_and_cultural_practices.name: Ritual arts
spiritual_and_cultural_practices.description: Kerala Tourism describes several traditional art forms as connected with worship and ritual, including Theyyam, Padayani, Theeyattu and Garudan Thookkam.

source.organization: Department of Tourism, Government of Kerala
source.title: Cultural Experience in Kerala

spiritual_and_cultural_practices.name: Religious diversity
spiritual_and_cultural_practices.description: Kerala Tourism highlights religious heritage including temples, churches, mosques and ritual traditions, reflecting the state's diverse religious and cultural landscape.

visitor_guidance: When attending a cultural or religious event, respect local traditions and follow the instructions of hosts, organizers, or venue authorities.
Kerala Tourism specifically advises visitors attending cultural events or festivals to dress modestly and avoid loud noises.
Do not treat ritual art forms as ordinary entertainment; some are connected with worship and religious practice.
Ask before photographing people, performers, rituals, or sacred spaces when local rules or sensitivities are unclear.
Do not assume a practice associated with one district, community, temple, church, mosque, or festival applies to all of Kerala.
Engage with local artists, performers, and craftspeople respectfully and avoid treating cultural traditions only as tourist spectacles.
